<thought>All subnetworks are series chains that can be linked together. Subnet 1 provides two resistors (R1 = 2.222 Ω, R2 = 4.445 Ω) from A → N1 → X1. Subnet 2 is a four‑resistor series (each 5 Ω) between X1 and X2 with intermediate nodes N_b1, N_b2, N_b3. Subnet 3 adds four resistors (R7 = 5 Ω, R8 = 10 Ω, R9 = 15 Ω, R10 = 20 Ω) from X2 through N_c1‑N_c3 to X3. Subnet 4 finishes the path with three resistors (R11 = 10 Ω, R12 = 15 Ω, R13 = 20 Ω) from X3 to B. This yields the required 13 resistors and matches the node names appearing in the measurement set.</thought>
